title: Runtime Tracing with TracePoint
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of runtime tracing with tracepoint in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply runtime tracing with tracepoint in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to overhead and safe use and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Runtime Tracing with TracePoint through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding runtime tracing with tracepoint helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Runtime Tracing with TracePoint helps you reason about observing runtime events. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Observing runtime events. Then connect it to Investigating method calls and exceptions. The remaining syllabus points—Debugging instrumentation, Overhead and safe use—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports runtime tracing with tracepoint. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for runtime tracing with tracepoint using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Overhead and safe use), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain runtime tracing with tracepoint, identify its place in advanced language features and metaprogramming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
